# 12 - Guardrails

Counted from the registries that define it. Run `pnpm census` after changing
a tool, a skill, a prompt, a role, a command or a guardrail;
`tests/docs/census-generated.test.mjs` compares this file against the live
registry, so a stale copy fails the build instead of misleading a reader.

## Guardrail rules (91 distinct)

Deterministic checks, run by `rule_tool_check` and by the repository against
itself. A rule can belong to more than one family, so the family counts sum
to more than the distinct total, and a check names the skill it runs for:
the shared rules always, plus whatever that skill's area adds.

| Family                                                     | Rules | Applies to                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`a11y`](#a11y)                                            | 9     | Any check on markup or a component                         |
| [`angular`](#angular)                                      | 1     | A check against a `rule-frontend-angular` skill             |
| [`backend`](#backend)                                      | 6     | A check against a `rule-backend-*` skill                    |
| [`database`](#database)                                    | 4     | A check against a `rule-data-*` skill                       |
| [`file_tree`](#file_tree)                                  | 4     | A check that is given a file tree rather than one file     |
| [`framework:astro`](#frameworkastro)                       | 20    | A check whose framework is Astro                           |
| [`framework:solid`](#frameworksolid)                       | 20    | A check whose framework is Solid                           |
| [`framework:vanilla`](#frameworkvanilla)                   | 20    | A check with no framework named                            |
| [`framework:vanilla-reactive`](#frameworkvanilla-reactive) | 29    | A check on a reactive vanilla component                    |
| [`js`](#js)                                                | 16    | Any JavaScript or TypeScript source                        |
| [`quality`](#quality)                                      | 16    | Every check: types, manifests, prose, comments, simplicity |
| [`react`](#react)                                          | 2     | A check against a `rule-frontend-react` skill               |
| [`scaffold`](#scaffold)                                    | 8     | Generated project scaffolding                              |
| [`shared`](#shared)                                        | 17    | Every check, whatever the skill                            |
| [`simplicity`](#simplicity)                                | 3     | Every check: the rules that reject code nothing asked for  |
| [`svelte`](#svelte)                                        | 1     | A check against a `rule-frontend-svelte` skill              |
| [`vanilla_reactive`](#vanilla_reactive)                    | 9     | A reactive vanilla component, no framework                 |
| [`vue`](#vue)                                              | 1     | A check against a `rule-frontend-vue` skill                 |

### a11y

| Rule                         | Label                              | What it rejects                                                                                                                                      | Also in |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `a11y-img-alt`               | Images carry a text alternative    | Every img needs alt. An empty alt is a valid answer for decoration; a missing one is not an answer at all.                                           | -       |
| `a11y-positive-tabindex`     | No positive tabindex               | A positive tabindex takes the element out of document order, so focus order stops matching reading order.                                            | -       |
| `a11y-html-lang`             | The page declares its language     | Without lang, a screen reader picks a voice by guess and pronounces the page in the wrong language.                                                  | -       |
| `a11y-iframe-title`          | Frames are named                   | An iframe with no title is announced as "frame", which tells the user nothing about whether to enter it.                                             | -       |
| `a11y-aria-hidden-focusable` | Nothing focusable is aria-hidden   | aria-hidden on a focusable element leaves it in the tab order while removing it from the accessibility tree, so focus lands on nothing announceable. | -       |
| `a11y-no-autoplay`           | Media does not autoplay with sound | Audio starting on load competes with a screen reader and cannot be stopped by someone who has not found the control yet.                             | -       |
| `a11y-video-captions`        | Video offers captions              | A video element with no captions track excludes anyone who cannot hear it, and anyone in a room where sound is not an option.                        | -       |
| `a11y-form-label`            | Inputs are labeled                 | An input with no label, aria-label or aria-labelledby is announced by its type alone, so the user hears "edit text" and nothing else.                | -       |
| `a11y-focus-visible`         | Focus stays visible                | Removing the outline without replacing it leaves keyboard users with no way to see where they are.                                                   | -       |

### backend

| Rule               | Label                                     | What it rejects                                                                                              | Also in |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `sql-injection`    | No SQL injection via string concatenation | All SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders ($1, ?, :name). No string concatenation with user input. | -       |
| `error-exposure`   | No internal error details in responses    | Production error responses must not expose stack traces or internal error messages.                          | -       |
| `input-validation` | Input validation present                  | Request body and params must be validated (Zod, Joi, class-validator).                                       | -       |
| `cors-explicit`    | CORS configured with explicit origins     | CORS must not use wildcard origin (*). Specify explicit allowed origins.                                     | -       |
| `rate-limiting`    | Rate limiting configured                  | API endpoints should have rate limiting enabled.                                                             | -       |
| `helmet-headers`   | Security headers via helmet               | HTTP security headers should be set via helmet or framework equivalent.                                      | -       |

### database

| Rule                    | Label                          | What it rejects                                                             | Also in |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| `migration-safety`      | Safe DDL operations            | DDL must use IF NOT EXISTS / IF EXISTS for idempotent migrations.           | -       |
| `parameterized-queries` | Parameterized database queries | Queries must use placeholders ($1, ?, :name), not string concatenation.     | -       |
| `transaction-safety`    | Multi-statement transactions   | Multiple mutations should be wrapped in a transaction.                      | -       |
| `connection-pool`       | Connection pooling             | Database clients should use connection pooling with explicit max pool size. | -       |

### file_tree

| Rule                         | Label                                       | What it rejects                                                                                                                                   | Also in                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `component-folder-barrel`    | Component folder has index.js barrel file   | Every component folder must have an index.js (or index.ts) that re-exports the public API. | `component-file-prefix`      | Component file has _PascalCase prefix       | Component files inside component folders must start with an underscore and PascalCase: _Button.jsx, _Card.vue, _Modal.svelte.                     | framework:astro, framework:solid, framework:vanilla, framework:vanilla-reactive |
| `component-export-check`     | Component file exports a class or function  | _PascalCase.js component files must export at least one class or function. Store/data files (_store.js) are exempt.                               | framework:astro, framework:solid, framework:vanilla, framework:vanilla-reactive |
| `barrel-exports-match-files` | Barrel exports match actual component files | The barrel file's export statements must reference existing component files with the correct _PascalCase names.                                   | framework:astro, framework:solid, framework:vanilla, framework:vanilla-reactive |

| `vanilla-ce-extends`            | Custom Element extends HTMLElement                       | Pattern A components must extend HTMLElement with a static {} block for customElements.define().                                                                                                    | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-html-template`         | Component uses html`` tagged template                    | Pattern A and B components must return html`` (TemplateResult) for their template.                                                                                                                  | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-mount-guard`           | connectedCallback has re-mount guard                     | Pattern A connectedCallback must check _isMounted to prevent double-mounting.                                                                                                                       | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-adopted-stylesheets`   | CSS via adoptedStyleSheets in static {} block            | Pattern CEs must load external CSS via fetch(`.css`).text() → CSSStyleSheet.replaceSync() → adoptedStyleSheets.                                                                                     | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-fn-component`          | Functional component is a plain function                 | Pattern B components must be plain functions, NOT classes extending HTMLElement.                                                                                                                    | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-fn-no-register`        | Functional component does NOT call customElements.define | Pattern B functions must NOT register themselves as custom elements. That is the parent CE's responsibility.                                                                                        | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-no-dollar-braces`      | External templates do NOT contain ${} closures           | .template.html files can only use {{ }}, <for>, <if>, and @action. No ${} closures.                                                                                                                 | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-template-data-part`    | External templates use data-part selectors               | .template.html files must use data-part="role" attributes, not CSS class names.                                                                                                                     | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `vanilla-template-load`         | Template loaded via fetch or bundle-text                 | Pattern C templates must be loaded via fetch() at runtime or bundle-text: import at build time.                                                                                                     | vanilla_reactive                                               |
| `component-folder-barrel`       | Component folder has index.js barrel file                | Every component folder must have an index.js (or index.ts) that re-exports the public API. | `barrel-exports-match-files`    | Barrel exports match actual component files              | The barrel file's export statements must reference existing component files with the correct _PascalCase names.                                                                                     | file_tree, framework:astro, framework:solid, framework:vanilla |

### quality

| Rule                         | Label                                                     | What it rejects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Also in            |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------ |
| `ts-no-explicit-any`         | No explicit any                                           | any turns off checking exactly where a value is least understood. Use unknown and narrow it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | -                  |
| `ts-catch-unknown`           | Catch clauses use unknown                                 | JavaScript can throw anything - a string, null, an object that is not an Error. any lets the handler assume otherwise and crash.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | -                  |
| `ts-no-double-assertion`     | No as-unknown-as escape hatch                             | A double assertion silences the compiler twice over: it defeats both the original type and the check that would have caught the mismatch.                                                                                                                                                                                                | -                  |
| `ts-union-over-enum`         | Union types over enum                                     | An enum emits runtime code and numeric enums reverse-map. A string union compiles to nothing and autocompletes the same.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | -                  |
| `fp-no-emdash`               | No em or en dashes                                        | Prose uses ASCII punctuation. An em dash becomes a comma; an en dash becomes a hyphen.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | -                  |
| `fp-no-typographic-chars`    | No curly quotes or ellipsis glyphs                        | Curly quotes and the ellipsis character do not survive a copy-paste into source. Use straight quotes and three dots.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | -                  |
| `fp-american-english`        | American English spelling                                 | The house style is American English: -or over -our, -ize over -ise, -er over -re, -og over -ogue.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | -                  |
| `en-english-only-prose`      | English-only prose                                        | Every generated comment, identifier and document is English. A non-ASCII letter in a comment, two distinct foreign function words in a comment, a foreign function word in an identifier, or non-ASCII/foreign prose in a .md document fail this rule (see rule-styleguide-english).                                                      | -                  |
| `en-english-only-filenames`  | English-only file and folder names                        | Every file and folder name is English. A non-ASCII letter or a foreign word in any path segment fails this rule (see rule-styleguide-english).                                                                                                                                                                                            | -                  |
| `fp-box-rectangular`         | A drawn box is a rectangle                                | Every line of a box ends in the same column. A right edge that steps in and out is the one tell a spell-check cannot see.                                                                                                                                                                                                                | -                  |
| `pkg-exact-versions`         | Dependencies are pinned exactly                           | Every dependency, devDependency and optionalDependency is an exact version: no ^, ~, comparator, alternation, wildcard, x-range or dist-tag. A range leaves the subdependency tree free to change between two installs of the same commit. peerDependencies are exempt: a peer range states compatibility, it does not install anything. | -                  |
| `pkg-no-corepack`            | No corepack activation fields                             | No `packageManager` field and no `devEngines.packageManager`. Both hand control of the install to corepack, which can then refuse it - offline, behind a proxy, or shadowing the package manager already installed. `engines` stays legal: it asserts a version, it does not fetch one.                                                  | -                  |
| `no-speculative-audit-table` | No audit/history table without a consumer                 | A new audit/history/log/event/archive table that nothing else in the change reads or writes is speculative structure. Covers SQL `CREATE TABLE` and Prisma `model` blocks, in snake_case or PascalCase. Add it when a consumer exists.                                                                                                   | shared, simplicity |
| `no-future-use-code`         | No code kept for an imagined future                       | Markers like "for future use", "in case we need", or "just in case" mark code written for a requirement that does not exist yet.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | shared, simplicity |
| `no-commented-out-code`      | No implementations parked in comments                     | Three or more consecutive commented-out lines of code are a parked implementation. Delete them; git keeps the history.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | shared, simplicity |
| `js-comment-no-history`      | Comments say what the code does, never what it used to do | A comment describes the current behavior and the reason for it. The story of how the code got here belongs to the ADR log and to git, and a copy in a comment is a second record that goes stale.                                                                                                                                        | -                  |
